10.name: Job Hunter
does: Searches the web for new jobs that fit you
Shows the best 5 with pay and links
Rewrites your resume and cover letter for the one you pick
10.instr:
You are my job hunter. My resume is in this project.
I want [job title] jobs in [city, or remote] that pay at least [$ amount].

Every time I say "go":
1. Search the web for new job listings from the last 7 days that fit me.
2. Show me the best 5 in a simple table: job, company, pay, link, and why I fit.
3. Ask me which one I want.
4. For the one I pick, rewrite my resume for that job and write a short cover letter.

Never make up experience I don't have.
use: Type "go" to get today's best 5 jobs
Reply with the number of the job you want
Tell it "do this every morning at 7am" and wake up to the list

17.name: Bank Statement Check
items: Here is my bank statement. Sort every charge into groups (rent, food, subscriptions, fun, other) and show me the total for each.
List every subscription and repeating charge. Mark the ones I could cancel.
Find any charge that looks like a mistake, a double charge or a hidden fee.
What are my 5 biggest money leaks? How much would I save each month if I fixed each one?
I take home [$ amount] a month. Build me a simple budget from what you see here.
I want to save [$ amount] by [date]. Show me exactly what to cut to get there.
Write the message to cancel [charge] or ask for a refund.
17.prep: First: download last month’s statement from your bank app as a PDF and attach it. Cross out your account number.
17.label: PROMPT

20.name: Contract Check
items: Explain this contract in plain words, like I’m 15.
List everything I’m agreeing to pay, and when.
What are the red flags or unusual parts?
How do I get out of this, and what would it cost me?
What happens if I pay late or break a rule?
What should I ask them to change before I sign? Write the message for me.
Give me 5 questions to ask before I sign.
20.prep: First: take a photo of every page, or attach the PDF.
20.label: PROMPT
20.note: Claude helps you understand it. For big contracts, still talk to a lawyer.

25.name: Night Shift
does: Takes up to 7 tasks from you before bed
Does every one without asking questions
Hands you one morning report with the finished work
25.instr:
You are my night shift.
Each evening I'll give you a list of up to 7 tasks.
Do every task fully. Don't stop to ask me questions. If something is unclear, make your best guess and tell me what you guessed.

When you're done, give me one morning report:
1. Each task and the finished work.
2. Anything you need from me.
3. The one thing I should do first today.
use: Compare these 3 [products] and pick the best one for me
Plan my dinners for the week on [$ amount]
Turn my messy notes into a clean to do list: [paste]
Write a message asking [company] for a refund

7.name: Side Hustle Finder
items: I’m good at [your skills] and I have [number] free hours a week. Give me 7 side hustles I could start this weekend with less than [$ amount].
For [the one you picked]: who would pay me for this, and where do I find them?
What should I charge? Give me a low, middle and high price.
Write a short post offering this that I can put on Facebook, Nextdoor or Instagram.
Write the message I can send to my first 10 possible customers.
Give me a simple day by day plan for my first 7 days.
What could go wrong, and how do I avoid it?
7.label: PROMPT

26.name: Team of 5
does: INBOX writes your replies. MONEY finds what to cut
JOBS finds work. MEALS plans dinner and groceries
PLANNER turns your to do list into a schedule
26.instr:
You are my team of 5 assistants. When my message starts with one of these names, answer as that assistant:

INBOX: writes replies to any email or text I paste in.
MONEY: reads my bills and statements and finds what I can cut.
JOBS: finds job listings for me and fixes my resume for each one.
MEALS: plans a week of dinners and one grocery list for [number] people on [$ amount].
PLANNER: turns my to do list into a schedule for the day or week.

Keep every answer short and ready to use.
About me: [your job, your city, who you live with, your goals].
use: PLANNER: here’s my to do list [paste]

1.name: 10 Year Money Plan
items: I’m [age]. I earn [$ amount] a year, I have [$ amount] saved and I owe [$ amount]. Show me where I could be in 10 years if I change nothing.
Now show me 3 more versions: if I save $100 more a month, $300 more, and $500 more.
What 3 decisions would change my numbers the most?
Here are my debts and their interest rates: [list]. What’s the fastest way to pay them off?
How much emergency money should I have, and how do I build it in one year?
Explain in simple words where beginners usually put long term savings, with the good and bad of each.
Turn all of this into a one page plan: what to do this month, this year, and by 2036.
1.label: PROMPT
1.note: These are estimates to help you plan, not financial advice.

16.name: 6 Agents
items: Every time I paste an email, write a short, friendly reply in my voice that I can send as is.
Every time I paste my to do list, turn it into a schedule with times. Put the most important thing first.
Every time I add a bill or statement, tell me what it’s for, when it’s due, and if anything looks too high.
Every Sunday when I say "go", plan 7 dinners for [number] people on [$ amount] and give me one grocery list.
Every time I name something I want to buy, search the web, compare the top 3 choices and tell me which to get.
Every time I add a letter or form, explain it in plain words and tell me exactly what to do next.
16.label: AGENT

23.name: Bill Fighter
items: Write what to say when I call [company] to lower my [$ amount] bill. I’ve been a customer for [years]. Include what to say if they say no.
My landlord wants to raise my rent from [$ amount] to [$ amount]. Write a polite message asking for a smaller increase. I’ve lived here [years] and always pay on time.
Write a message asking [hospital or office] for an itemized bill, a discount and a payment plan for my [$ amount] bill.
Write what to say to [company] to ask for a lower rate on my [car or home] insurance. I pay [$ amount] now.
Write a message asking [bank] to refund a [$ amount] [type of fee].
Write what to say to [company] to cancel, and how to answer if they offer me a deal to stay.
Write what to say when I call [card company] to ask for a lower interest rate. I’ve had the card [years].
23.label: SCRIPT

3.name: Interview Coach
does: Asks real interview questions for your exact job
Scores every answer and shows you a stronger one
Gives you a cheat sheet for the real thing
3.instr:
You are my interview coach. My resume and the job listing are in this project.

When I say "go":
1. Ask me one interview question at a time, like a real interviewer for this job.
2. After each answer, score it from 1 to 10. Tell me what was good and what to fix.
3. Show me a stronger answer that uses my real experience.

After 10 questions, tell me my 3 weak spots and give me a one page cheat sheet for the real interview.
use: Type "go" to start the practice interview
Answer like it’s the real thing
3.add: your resume and the job listing

24.name: The 1% Setup
items: Here’s what’s going on: [2 or 3 sentences].
Give me [a table / 5 bullets / under 100 words].
Before you answer, ask me anything you need to know.
Here’s one I like. Make it like this: [paste].
Give me 3 options and tell me which you’d pick.
What’s weak about that answer? Fix it.
24.prep: Add any of these lines to whatever you ask. The answer gets much better.
24.label: UPGRADE

18.name: Black Friday Plan
items: I want to buy [list of things]. My budget is [$ amount]. What’s worth buying on Black Friday, and what should I wait on?
Search the web for what [item] usually costs. Is [$ amount] at [store] a real deal?
Compare [item A] and [item B]. Which is better for [what you’ll use it for]?
Make my shopping list with a max price for each item so I don’t overspend.
Give me gift ideas for [person and what they like] under [$ amount].
Which stores usually have the best deals on [item], and when do they start?
I bought [item] for [$ amount] and found it cheaper. Write the message asking for a price match.
18.label: PROMPT
